root_cause.text: The BPF JIT allocator was requesting only 4-byte alignment (sizeof(u32)) instead of 8-byte alignment for the JIT buffer, causing the u64 target field in struct bpf_plt to potentially be misaligned, which breaks the atomicity guarantee required for concurrent 64-bit loads on ARM64.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the alignment parameter in bpf_jit_binary_pack_alloc() from `sizeof(u32)` to `sizeof(u64)`. The CVE description explicitly states that "64-bit loads/stores are only guaranteed to be single-copy atomic if they are 64-bit aligned" on ARM64, and that with 4-byte alignment, the base address could end in 0x4 or 0xc, preventing the relative padding logic in build_plt() from ensuring the target field lands on an 8-byte boundary. This misalignment allows concurrent WRITE_ONCE() updates in bpf_arch_text_poke() to tear the 64-bit read, causing the JIT to jump to a corrupted address.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix BPF JIT compilation by correcting the read-only image alignment from 32-bit to 64-bit boundaries.
intent_record.what: Changed the alignment parameter in bpf_jit_binary_pack_alloc() from sizeof(u32) to sizeof(u64) on line 2122.
intent_record.how: This increases the memory alignment requirement for the JIT-compiled BPF program's read-only image from 4-byte to 8-byte boundaries. This affects how the binary pack allocator positions the read-only image in memory, ensuring stricter alignment that may be required for correct execution on 64-bit architectures or for performance optimization.

grouping_result.intent: Fix BPF JIT compilation by correcting the read-only image alignment from 32-bit to 64-bit boundaries.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the root cause by fixing the alignment of the BPF JIT buffer from 4-byte (32-bit) to 8-byte (64-bit) boundaries. This ensures proper alignment of the u64 target field in struct bpf_plt, which is exactly what the vulnerability root cause identifies as the problem causing misalignment and breaking atomicity guarantees for concurrent 64-bit loads on ARM64.

candidates.rationale: The bpf_jit_binary_pack_alloc call passes sizeof(u32) (4-byte alignment) as the alignment parameter for the read-only JIT buffer. This is insufficient for the u64 target field in struct bpf_plt, which requires 8-byte alignment to guarantee atomic 64-bit loads on ARM64. The root cause is directly in this alignment argument.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement passes sizeof(u32) (4-byte alignment) to bpf_jit_binary_pack_alloc as the alignment parameter for the read-only JIT buffer. The u64 target field in struct bpf_plt requires 8-byte alignment to guarantee atomic 64-bit loads on ARM64. The insufficient 4-byte alignment causes potential misalignment of the u64 field, breaking the atomicity guarantee required for concurrent access on ARM64 architecture.

bpf, arm64: use bpf_prog_pack for memory management

Use bpf_jit_binary_pack_alloc for memory management of JIT binaries
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 1dad391daef129e01e28206b8d586608ff026548
Author: Puranjay Mohan <puranjay@kernel.org>
Date:   Wed Feb 28 14:18:24 2024 +0000

    bpf, arm64: use bpf_prog_pack for memory management
    
    Use bpf_jit_binary_pack_alloc for memory management of JIT binaries in
    ARM64 BPF JIT. The bpf_jit_binary_pack_alloc creates a pair of RW and RX
    buffers. The JIT writes the program into the RW buffer. When the JIT is
    done, the program is copied to the final RX buffer
    with bpf_jit_binary
bic_trace_step.reason: Line 1674-1676 shows the vulnerable call to bpf_jit_binary_pack_alloc with alignment parameter set to sizeof(u32) (4 bytes): 'ro_header = bpf_jit_binary_pack_alloc(image_size, &ro_image_ptr, sizeof(u32), &header, &image_ptr, jit_fill_hole);'. According to the vulnerability root cause, this should be 8-byte alignment (sizeof(u64)) to ensure proper alignment of the u64 target field in struct bpf_plt for ARM64, which requires 8-byte alignment for atomic 64-bit loads. The code passes sizeof(u32) as the alignment parameter, which is insufficient and introduces the misalignment vulnerability. This is the bug-introducing commit where the incorrect alignment was introduced when switching to bpf_prog_pack for memory management.

The JIT compiler emits A64 instructions. It supports eBPF only.
Legacy BPF is supported thanks
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit e54bcde3d69d40023ae77727213d14f920eb264a
Author: Zi Shen Lim <zlim.lnx@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Aug 26 21:15:30 2014 -0700

    arm64: eBPF JIT compiler
    
    The JIT compiler emits A64 instructions. It supports eBPF only.
    Legacy BPF is supported thanks to conversion by BPF core.
    
    JIT is enabled in the same way as for other architectures:
    
            echo 1 > /proc/sys/net/core/bpf_jit_enable
    
    Or for additional compiler output:
    
            echo 2 > /proc/sys
bic_trace_step.reason: Line 643 shows the vulnerable construct: 'image_size = sizeof(u32) * ctx.idx;' followed by line 644 'ctx.image = module_alloc(image_size);'. The code allocates the JIT buffer using only 4-byte alignment (sizeof(u32)) instead of the required 8-byte alignment for ARM64. This causes the u64 target field in struct bpf_plt to be potentially misaligned, breaking the atomicity guarantee for concurrent 64-bit loads on ARM64. The allocation does not enforce 8-byte alignment, and there is no fix present in this code to address the alignment requirement.
